online-stopwatch.quickAnswer: Press start and the stopwatch counts up with centisecond precision. Hit lap to record split times without stopping - each lap shows its own duration and the running total, and the fastest and slowest laps are highlighted automatically.
keyFacts: A stopwatch counts up from zero; a timer counts down to zero - this tool is the former.
Centisecond precision (1/100th of a second) is plenty for sports, cooking and experiments.
A lap records a split time without stopping the main clock, so you can time segments of one run.
Browser intervals tick roughly every 10 ms; the display is precise but not laboratory-grade.
Fastest and slowest laps are highlighted so patterns jump out at a glance.
howTo: Press Lap anytime to record a split without stopping.
Press Pause to freeze the clock; Resume continues from the same point.
Press Reset to clear the time and all laps.
Compare lap rows - green marks the fastest, red the slowest.
online-stopwatch.formula:
Elapsed = number of 10 ms ticks x 10 ms.
Lap time = lap total minus previous lap total.
Display = MM:SS.CS (minutes, seconds, centiseconds).
Example: 90.25 s -> 01:30.25.
online-stopwatch.workedExample:
Timing a run with 3 laps:
1. Start -> run -> Lap at 01:30.25 (lap 1 = 90.25 s, total 90.25 s).
2. Continue -> Lap at 03:05.10 (lap 2 = 94.85 s, total 185.10 s).
3. Continue -> Pause at 04:40.00 (lap 3 = 94.90 s, total 280.00 s).
4. Fastest: lap 1 (90.25 s). Slowest: lap 3 (94.90 s).
Total time: 4 minutes 40 seconds.
benefits: Time anything - runs, recipes, study blocks, speeches - with one click.
Laps reveal pacing: are you fading in later segments?
No app install and no account; works offline once loaded.
Clean, distraction-free display readable at a glance.
limitations: Browser timing is approximate at the millisecond level; not suitable for official races.
Closing or reloading the tab resets the stopwatch and clears laps.
There is no sound or vibration alert - watch the display.
Very long runs (many hours) keep counting but the display is not optimized for them.

faqs.a: It ticks every 10 milliseconds (centisecond precision). That is plenty for training, cooking and experiments, but not for certified competitions.

faqs.q: What is the difference between lap and total?
faqs.a: Lap time is the duration of that segment alone; total is the elapsed time since you pressed start. Both are shown for every lap.

faqs.q: Can I pause without losing laps?
faqs.a: Yes. Pause freezes everything; Resume continues from the same elapsed time with all laps intact.

faqs.q: Why is one lap green and one red?
faqs.a: Green marks your fastest lap and red your slowest (when you have 2+ laps), so pacing patterns are visible instantly.

faqs.q: Can I export my lap times?
faqs.a: Not in this version - note down or screenshot the laps you want to keep before resetting.
